q: Why did CAC increase yesterday? Check whether the change came from CPM, CTR, CPC, landing-page conversion, checkout conversion, product mix, or channel mix. Rank the drivers by likely contribution.
answer:
Yesterday CAC was ₹2,102 (about +8.3% vs its recent same-weekday “usual”), but the diagnosis found no single statistically supported cause — the movement looks like ordinary variation with a mix shift toward Meta that explains most of the arithmetic change. 

- Top-ranked contributors (arithmetic decomposition, not proven causal claims):  
  1) Channel mix (shift toward Meta): Meta CAC rose (≈₹2,390 → ₹2,900) and Meta ad spend +49% with much larger sales lift inside Meta; this mix shift explains the largest share of the day-to-day CAC movement.  
  2) Ad spend vs new customers (volume effect): Brand ad spend rose while new customers also rose; ad spend and new-customer changes together produced the observed CAC change (Ad spend ₹50,442 yesterday; New customers 24).  
  3) Funnel rates and marketplace-level media rates (CPM/CTR/CPC/Landing-page cost/checkout conversion): CPM ↑ ~18%, CTR ↑ ~11%, CPC ↑ ~6%, cost-per-LPV ↓ ~12%, checkout rate ↑ ~63% — each moved but stayed within their normal ranges and none was flagged as a statistically supported cause.  
  4) Product mix: orders containing the product rose (26 → 45, +73%) but this was within its usual range and the engine ruled it out as a supported cause.

Worth checking: run a campaign-level drilldown for Meta yesterday to confirm which campaigns/ads increased spend or drove the higher new-customer count.
